title: Bare Wafer Inspection - ESD Damage Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify ESD Damage defects during post-cmp inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for ESD Damage defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Bare Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: ESD Damage
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-cmp monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v11.1.228
Recipe: BARE_WAFER_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (139 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Bare Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target ESD Damage defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 95 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 97% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for Bare Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.97 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-05-29
Wafers Tested: 24
Total Defects Found: 743
Defect Density: 236.5 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.0%
Capture Rate: 91.3%
Test Duration: 264 minutes
System Uptime: 99.2%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting ESD Damage at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
